Then Jāwalī, when he had abandoned Raḥbuth,
went and encamped against Callinicus (Raqqa),
and waged war against it for many days.
Now Sultan Ghiyāth al-Dīn sent to him a certain emir named Ḥusayn ibn Atabeg,
demanding that he submit and return to Mosul under his appointment as he had been before.
And he did not obey,
but went and encamped against Bālis, subdued it, plundered it,
and wrought great devastation in it.
Then Riḍwān, the lord of Syria,
becoming distressed because Jāwalī had ravaged his lands,
sent and requested help from Tancred, the king (prince) of Antioch.
And he came to him with one thousand five hundred Frankish horsemen,
and six hundred Turkish horsemen of those of Riḍwān.
And Jāwalī also sent to Baldwin and Joscelin, that they might come to his aid.
And when they came,
battle was joined near Tell Bāshir, and the Franks and Turks of Riḍwān prevailed over the Franks and Turks of Jāwalī,
and routed them.
And many of the Turks in the center were killed,
because the Franks would not kill the Franks,
but only cast them down from their horses.
And Baldwin and Joscelin fled and entered Tell Bāshir,
and with them were some of the Turks from Jāwalī's party.
And when they had tended to their wounds,
they sent them to Jāwalī.
Then Jāwalī, when he was defeated,
found no way out for himself
except to take refuge once again in the mercy of the Sultan.
And with a few men,
having disguised himself
and concealed his name,
he swiftly traveled from Syria to Khorasan,
three hundred and sixty parasangs in 17 days. And when he reached the camp of the Sultan, he said to the guards of the roads:
"I am Jāwalī,
and I desire that you bring me to the tent of the emir Ḥusayn,"
the one who had been sent to him by the Sultan while he was encamped against Raḥbuth.
And Ḥusayn took him
and brought him before the Sultan, while carrying his burial shroud.
And the Sultan had compassion on him and granted him a pledge of safety,
and he entered his service.
Now Bazmīsh, when he had taken the wife of Qilij Arslān from Mosul and gone to Melitene,
proclaimed Ṭughril Arslān, the younger son of Qilij Arslān, as king.
